Johannes Brahms. The German composer, pianist, and conductor who was one of the leading musicians of the Romantic period.

Often grouped with Bach and Beethoven as one of the Three Bs of classical music, Brahms was a musical traditionalist. He championed Classical structures, sonata form, and strict counterpoint. He placed himself in opposition to the progressive New German School of Franz Liszt and Richard Wagner.

Highly self-critical, Brahms destroyed many of his early drafts and spent over twenty years perfecting his First Symphony. When it was completed, it was immediately hailed as a masterpiece. The conductor Hans von Bülow famously dubbed it Beethoven's Tenth, referencing both the shadow of Beethoven under which Brahms composed and the similarity of the finale's grand major-key theme to the Ode to Joy.

A German Requiem, subtitled Ein deutsches Requiem, is a massive sacred choral work. Unlike the traditional Latin Catholic liturgy, it sets German Lutheran biblical texts. He wrote it following the deaths of his mother and his mentor Robert Schumann.

The Academic Festival Overture is a boisterous concert overture composed as a thank-you to the University of Breslau for awarding him an honorary doctorate. It weaves together popular nineteenth-century student drinking songs and concludes with Gaudeamus igitur.

Brahms wrote Hungarian Dances, a highly popular set of twenty-one dance tunes based on Hungarian Romani melodies. Originally written for piano four-hands, the most famous is No. 5 in F-sharp minor.

His Lullaby, or Wiegenlied, is his universally recognized cradle song, composed to celebrate the birth of a friend's child.

Clara Schumann was the widow of Robert Schumann, with whom Brahms maintained a lifelong, deeply affectionate relationship. He acted as her confidant and assistant.

Robert Schumann was Brahms's closest mentor. Schumann declared the young Brahms to be a genius in the article Neue Bahnen and remained his most important influence. Brahms's counterpoint was mathematically rigorous, utilizing mirror inversions and complex canon structures.
